results.prompt: Explain the difference between RAM and SSD to a non-technical person.
results.response: Let's imagine your computer as if it were a kitchen where you prepare meals (or run programs). In this analogy, think of Random Access Memory or RAM like the blender on your countertop - when making smoothies quickly and often, its speed is crucial because every time I make another one while using an old mixture still in there slows down my work. Now imagine SSD as a refrigerator where you store ingredients (or save files). It's faster to take out items from the fridge when needed rather than rummaging through bins or cabinets, but it takes time for things like eggs and milk to chill in there before use. That’s why having RAM helps your computer work fast on active tasks while an SSD gives a quicker access overall once everything is cool (or ready).

results.prompt: You are an AI architect. Outline a high-level design for a modular AI assistant system.
results.response:
The proposed High Level Design (HLD) plan details the architecture of Modular_AI, which is designed as follows:

1. Service Layer: The service layer acts as an interface between different components and modules within our Assistant System providing services to users or other applications while abstracting away their internal workings from each other. This includes intent recognition for understanding user requests/commands, entity extraction with NLP techniques that identifies important entities (people names, dates etc.) in the input strings as well as dialogue management which controls flow of conversation between a user and Assistant.

2. AI Module: The core functionality resides within this module comprising Natural Language Understanding(NLU), Dialogue state tracking (DST) models that maintain context across multiple turns, Sentiment Analysis for understanding emotions behind requests/commands to better respond accordingly along with the Integration of Knowledge Graphs and Entity Recognition systems.

3. Data Processing Layer: This layer is responsible for cleaning raw data received from various channels like voice or text input before it gets processed by AI module. It includes noise reduction, speech-to-text conversion if required along with language detection (for multilingual support) and normalization of user’table inputs through preprocessing techniques to improve model performance.

4. Data Storage & Management Layer: This layer manages the storage, retrieval as well as updating/deletion activities for data associated with users such as their personal information, interaction logs etc., providing high availability and fault tolerance along with appropriate security mechanisms in place to safeguard sensitive user details from unauthorized access.
 
5. Infrastructure Layer: This consists of microservices orchestrated using container technology like Docker/Kubernetes which ensures flexibility, scalability & resilience by being able to deploy multiple instances across different environments while maintaining a consistent state and seamless failover in case one goes down.
 
6. Integration Layer: This layer is responsible for integrating various external APIs or services (like calendar, email client etc.) which are essential requirements of some commands/requests as well ensuring smooth data transfer between layers via API gateways with rate limiting and throttling mechanisms in place to ensure system stability even under heavy load scenarios.
 
7. User Interface: The final layer designed for providing a seamless, friendly user experience across web, mobile app or voice through respective front-end frameworks/technologies while maintaining the design consistency with brand guidelines and usability testing in place to iterate improvements based on real world usage patterns & feedback.
 
8. Deployment Pipeline: This includes continuous integration /continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines for automated deployment of changes across all layers ensuring faster rollouts, better traceability with version control tools like Git and maintaining proper documentation throughout the development process to keep everyone in sync about system updates & improvements made.
 
By dividing functionalities into distinctive modules it provides flexibility as developers can independently update or replace specific components without impact on other parts of the Assistant System thereby promoting faster innovation cycles while modular design also supports reuse and scalability for expanding business scope in future iterations, allowing additional features like multilingual support/localization to be easily integrated.
